title: Janapada of Vajji
capsule: Vajji (also Vrijji) was a confederate oligarchic republic of the northeastern Gangetic plain and one of the most powerful of the sixteen mahājanapadas, with its capital at Vaiśālī in modern north Bihar. It is historically exceptional as one of the earliest documented republican polities anywhere in the world, governed by an assembly (gaṇasaṅgha) of Licchavī, Videha, and allied clans; Buddhist sources record the Buddha delivering numerous discourses in Vaiśālī and praising its institutional strength. Magadha under Ajātaśatru (r. c. 492–460 BCE) waged a prolonged war against the confederation, reportedly introducing a new siege engine, and subjugated Vajji around 468 BCE, incorporating it as a Magadhan province.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The confederacy's core territory around Vaiśālī and north Bihar is reasonably established from Buddhist canonical texts and archaeology at the Kolhua site; the precise extent of its confederate territories is reconstructed from literary sources rather than defined archaeological boundaries.
